material_findings.finding: PyTorch eager CUDA support is distinct from current default Inductor/Triton support on native Windows SM7.5.
Stock PyTorch Adam stores scalar tensor step and does not directly encode elementwise birth-age.
Numba/NumPy mixed-type power promotion differs; explicit precision and state validation are required.
Graph replay omits Python work; target and Adam counters must advance through correct device mutation or staging.
NVIDIA's near-constant graph-launch example is Ampere-specific; pre-Ampere graph launch remains node-count dependent.
Batching token gradients into one optimizer step changes chronology; changed floating-point trajectories cannot inherit exact-replay claims.
CuPy14.2 setStream explicitly rejects non-HIP capturing streams. Stream capture API does not imply cuBLAS-backed matmul can be captured.
Elementwise multiply plus sum avoids this cuBLAS guard via ufunc/reduction paths. Entire-chain capture success and rounding equivalence still require an actual bounded test.
